subject: Request: Approve non-standard upfront-heavy payment & term discount for BlueHarbor
body:
From: Megan Collins <megan.collins@blueharbor.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
Cc: Daniel Reyes <daniel.reyes@blueharbor.com>, procurement@blueharbor.com
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Initial ask — multi-year prepay with front-loaded consumption

Hi Sofia,

Thanks again for the pilot. BlueHarbor is excited to commit but our CFO is pushing for a structure that puts most of the spend in year 1 to align with a capitalized budget this fiscal year. The ask: a 3-year term where ~65% of the committed spend is prepaid in year 1, then 20% in year 2, 15% in year 3.

Two constraints from procurement:
- We need a single signed agreement that covers all three years.
- Any deeper discounting needs executive approval on your side.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can (a) accept an upfront-heavy payment schedule, and (b) provide a steeper term discount for that shape? If so, what guardrails would you require on usage overage, termination, and invoice timing?

Attached: a rough usage forecast we expect.

Best,
Megan
Megan Collins
VP Finance, BlueHarbor Health

---

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Megan Collins <megan.collins@blueharbor.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 16 Apr 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial ask — multi-year prepay with front-loaded consumption

Hi Megan —

Appreciate the clarity. We can structure multi-year prepay and accept an upfront-heavy schedule, but for internal approval we'll need to validate pricing and risk around early consumption and potential churn. I copied Ben (sales lead) to help quantify the discount band and Vivek (finance) for approval flow.

High-level questions for you to confirm:
- Is BlueHarbor comfortable with a non-refundable prepay for the Year 1 portion?
- Do you expect material usage drop in years 2–3 (per your forecast)?

I attached a term sheet draft that shows a sample schedule and proposed overage rate. If that looks close, we'll kick this up for executive review.

Thanks,
Sofia
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: usage_forecast_blueharbor.xlsx

---

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 11:22:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Initial ask — multi-year prepay with front-loaded consumption

Team —

I reviewed BlueHarbor's forecast. Quick take: the ask is doable but it materially increases Redwood's revenue recognition and credit exposure. Proposed commercial options to present:

Option A (preferred by finance): 3-year term, Year1 prepaid 65%, Year2 20%, Year3 15%, 18% term discount on committed volume, overage at standard rate + 10%. Non-refundable Year1 prepay but we include a minimum utilization clause (e.g., 60% utilization threshold by end of Year1 or partial credit recapture).

Option B (sales-favorable): 3-year term, Year1 prepaid 65%, Year2 20%, Year3 15%, 22% term discount, overage at standard rate, but refundable portion of Year1 prepay capped at 15% if churn before Year2 with 90-day notice.

Risk to call out: Option B needs VP-level sign-off due to carve-outs and potential revenue restatements. Laura, can you advise on the level of approver we should loop in (VP/GM/CEO)?

Ben
Director, Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: redwood_term_sheet_v3.pdf

---

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 08:47:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Initial ask — multi-year prepay with front-loaded consumption

Ben, Sofia —

Finance perspective: Option A is acceptable with a couple of additions: (1) include a quarterly utilization review tied to deferred revenue amortization; (2) include a credit holdback mechanism triggered if utilization < 50% after Q1 of Year1; (3) require escrow or verified funds for the Year1 prepay if signed by procurement-only (no corporate guarantee). Option B is too aggressive on discounting and refundable language — escalates to me or CFO for approval.

Requesting: a one-page exec summary (1) framing expected NPV of the deal at each option, (2) proposed approver and sign-off thresholds, and (3) recommended guardrails for refund/recapture.

Vivek
Head of Finance, Redwood Inference

---

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2027 17:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial ask — multi-year prepay with front-loaded consumption

Vivek, Ben, Laura —

Thanks for the rapid feedback. I prepared the one-page exec summary (attached) and a recommended ask we can present to VP-level approval: Approve Option A as-is but allow Sales to offer Option B only if VP signs off after reviewing NPV and risk notes. The recommended commercial terms in the summary: 18% term discount, Year1 prepaid 65% non-refundable with utilization threshold (60% by end of Year1 or recapture schedule), overage at +10%, quarterly utilization reviews, and escrow for Year1 funds if procurement requires delayed corporate guarantee.

Please confirm approver and whether I can propose this structure directly to Megan this week. If Vivek or Laura want the VP/CFO escalation, let me know and I'll hold outreach until we have a named approver.

Thanks,
Sofia
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_exec_summary_bh_v1.pdf, redwood_term_sheet_v3.pdf
